userPresets.emptyHint: Import parameters from your own literature or measurements.
userPresets.modalSub: Enter biophysical parameters from your experimental measurements or literature source.
userPresets.fieldRadiusSub: µm — outer cell or capsid radius
userPresets.fieldEpsRSub: Effective dielectric constant of lipid bilayer (~5–15)
userPresets.fieldVmThrSub: V — transmembrane voltage at which irreversible EP occurs
userPresets.resonanceSectionSub: Required for resonance-mode targeting in acoustic disruption experiments.
userPresets.fieldResFreqSub: GHz — fundamental capsid or cell-wall resonant frequency
userPresets.fieldCapsidQSub: Mechanical Q (higher = sharper resonance; bacteria 3–5, virus 6–12)
userPresets.fieldResThrSub: V/cm — field amplitude at resonance required for disruption
userPresets.tipRadius: Cell Radius R [µm] Dominant size parameter in the Schwan equation. Vm ∝ R — larger cells charge to higher transmembrane voltages at the same field. Also sets the characteristic frequency: fc = 1/(2πτ), τ ∝ R. Typical ranges: mammalian 5–20 µm · bacteria 0.5–2 µm · virus 0.02–0.1 µm
userPresets.tipMemThick: Membrane Thickness d [nm] Sets membrane capacitance: Cm = ε_r·ε₀/d Thicker membrane → lower Cm → higher fc → field tolerance. Typical: mammalian 5–10 nm · bacteria wall 20–80 nm (use equivalent capacitive thickness).
userPresets.tipEpsR: Membrane Permittivity ε_r Effective dielectric constant of the lipid bilayer. Physical bilayer ε_r ≈ 2–5; NPC channels and proteins raise effective value to 5–15. Higher ε_r → higher Cm → lower fc → lower lysis field at DC.
userPresets.tipSigmaI: Intracellular Conductivity σ_i [S/m] Cytoplasm ionic conductivity. Affects τ and α (internal field factor for SAR). Typical: mammalian cytoplasm 0.4–1.5 S/m · gram-negative 0.3–0.5 S/m · gram-positive 0.2–0.4 S/m. High σ_i → lower τ (higher fc) → cell is harder to charge with short pulses.
userPresets.tipVmThr: Lysis Threshold Vm [V] Transmembrane voltage at which irreversible electroporation begins. DR = Vm / Vm_thr ≥ 0.85 triggers lysis in this model. Typical: mammalian 0.5–1.5 V · bacteria 0.8–2 V · virus (membrane disruption) 0.3–0.8 V. Ref: Weaver & Chizmadzhev (1996); Teissie & Rols (1993).
userPresets.tipDensity: Cell Density ρ [kg/m³] Used in SAR = σ_i·α²·E²·wf / ρ. Most mammalian cells ≈ 1000–1050 kg/m³ (close to water). Bacteria: ~1070 kg/m³. Viruses: ~1200–1400 kg/m³.
userPresets.tipCp: Specific Heat Capacity cp [J/(kg·K)] Used in temperature calculation: T_ss = 37 + SAR·dc / (λ·cp). Water: 4186. Mammalian cells: ~3500. Bacteria: ~3000. Dry virus particle: ~1000 (rarely relevant for in vitro).
userPresets.tipDerivedFc: Corner Frequency fc [kHz] Computed from your entered parameters and the current medium conductivity. fc = 1/(2πτ) τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) Below fc: Vm is at its Schwan maximum. Above fc: Vm falls as 1/f. This is the key frequency to operate below for maximum disruption.
userPresets.tipCellType: Cell Type Sets the physics mode used for targeting. Mammalian: Schwan transmembrane voltage model (IRE / selectivity mode). Bacteria: Schwan model + optional acoustic cell-wall resonance (GHz range). Virus: Acoustic capsid resonance model (GHz range) + Schwan approximation. Cell category is also auto-detected from radius: R < 0.1 µm → virus, R < 2 µm → bacteria.
userPresets.tipResFreq: Resonant Frequency f_res [GHz] Fundamental acoustic resonant frequency of the capsid or cell wall. For rigid-shell model: f_res ≈ v_sound / (2R) — using capsid speed of sound (~1500–3000 m/s). E. coli ~10–25 GHz · MRSA ~40–60 GHz · Influenza ~0.7 GHz · SARS-CoV-2 ~0.6 GHz. In practice these frequencies require rectangular waveguide or resonant cavity hardware.
userPresets.tipCapsidQ: Quality Factor Q Controls the sharpness of the resonance peak: bandwidth = f_res / Q. Higher Q → more frequency-selective disruption but tighter targeting bandwidth. Bacteria: Q ≈ 3–5 (viscoelastic peptidoglycan wall damps resonance). Virus: Q ≈ 6–12 (rigid capsid protein shell).
userPresets.tipResThr: Resonance Threshold [V/cm] Field amplitude at the resonant frequency required to achieve disruption. High-Q capsids need less field at resonance; low-Q bacteria need more. Estimate from literature acoustic disruption experiments. Typical range 500–15000 V/cm.
